inv.sub: The evidence and assumptions behind PulseCover. All figures are stated assumptions for a class project, not verified projections.
inv.seg1: Primary: health-conscious, digital-first people who own wearables and are underinsured, starting in the Klang Valley. Year 1 target: 5,000 policyholders through social, wearable-brand partnerships and referrals.
inv.seg2: Secondary: SME employers offering a voluntary group health and life benefit, a slower-ramping channel in Year 1.
inv.model.p: PulseCover is a digital broker / MGA for one licensed underwriting partner, avoiding the multi-year cost of a full BNM insurance licence. Revenue: 25% distribution commission on the RM600 base premium plus an optional RM5/month premium app subscription (20% take-up assumed).
inv.be.p: Breakeven is reached at about 23,591 policyholders against a 5,000 Year 1 target, expected in Years 2 to 3 as acquisition cost amortises and the risk pool scales.
inv.risk1: Securing a licensed underwriting partner who accepts wearable-informed pricing.
inv.risk2: Reaching enough opt-in scale before adverse selection erodes the model.
inv.risk3: Maintaining trust in biometric data handling: 77.8% of surveyed people cited privacy concerns.
prv.sub: Trust comes first. 77.8% of people worry about biometric privacy, so we treat governance as a precondition, not an afterthought.
prv.1p: Only daily steps, exercise minutes, sleep hours and resting heart rate from your linked device, plus the details you give us to issue your policy. We do not collect location, messages or contacts.
prv.2p: To calculate your health score and your renewal premium within the published ±15% band, and to give you in-app insights. Never to sell, advertise to you or share with employers.
prv.3p: Sharing is opt-in. You can pause tracking, disconnect your device or request a copy or deletion of your data at any time, subject to insurance record-keeping law.
prv.4p: Encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls, hashed passwords and a compliance lead who owns BNM and personal-data-protection obligations.
prv.5p: We publish our pricing method, cap changes at ±15%, reprice only at renewal and tell you before. No algorithm change without notice.
faq.q1: Do I need a medical exam?
faq.a1: No. Your wearable data replaces manual health declarations.
faq.q2: What if I do not own a wearable?
faq.a2: You can enter readings manually while you get a device. Wearable partners offer onboarding bundles for new policyholders.
faq.q3: Can my premium go up a lot?
faq.a3: No. The most it can move is 15% above the RM600 base, once a year at renewal, using a 12-month average.
faq.q4: I am under 18. Can I join?
faq.a4: Yes from age 16, with a parent or guardian named on the application.
faq.q5: Is there an upper age limit?
faq.a5: PulseCover is designed for every age group that uses a health tracker. Moderate activity like walking earns full marks.
faq.a6: A licensed partner insurer (Insurer Name Sdn Bhd) underwrites your policy. PulseCover operates as its registered broker / MGA.
faq.q7: What does the app subscription add?
faq.a7: An optional RM5/month for deeper insights and coaching. It never changes your insurance price.
faq.a8: File online, upload details, and follow each status live. No paper forms.
faq.a9: Fitbit, Garmin and Whoop, consolidated through Google Health Connect, on iOS and Android.
